statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON (green). Tail remains in the low band because the CME equity complex is still halted and the last observed tape was orderly, while Stress stays high on a pre-FOMC rates and energy backdrop carrying an unpriced weekend stack: a fatal Strait of Hormuz vessel strike, Iran-GCC talks in Salalah on Monday, and a Nasdaq-specific debate over the pace of AI development.
recommendation: Tail sits below the caution threshold, so the mapped state is EA_ON for both NQ futures and the NAS100 CFD. One narrow window is flagged: 21:00-02:00 UTC spanning the Globex reopen, where two days of unpriced Gulf and AI-sector headlines meet the thinnest liquidity of the week and the mapped state is WATCH.
headline: Nasdaq-100 closed and orderly into a hawkish Fed week, with a fatal Hormuz strike, Monday's Iran-GCC talks and an AI-pacing debate framing the Sunday reopen
body: CME equity futures remain shut until 22:00 UTC, so no live NQ price path exists at assessment time. The last observed tape is Friday's: the Nasdaq-100 closed at 29,368.44, up 0.91%, inside a 29,313.51-29,473.12 range and roughly 105 points below the session high, so the index was not pinned at an extreme, while VIX fell 11.21% to 15.84. That structure is orderly and retracement-friendly, which keeps Tail in the low band. The backdrop is tighter than the tape suggests. Treasury yields stand at 4.95% on the 10-year, 4.56% on the 2-year and 5.37% on the 30-year in the latest H.15 release, with reporting noting the 2-year touched 4.596% on Friday, its highest since July 2024, as a global bond selloff pushed the 10-year toward 5% on oil and rate-hike fears. WTI is near $100 and Brent near $104 after a sharp weekly gain, and Reuters reported traders pricing roughly a 72% chance of a hike at Wednesday's FOMC, up from 49% a week earlier, with the press conference half an hour after the decision. Equities near record highs with VIX under 16 against that stack is a thin cushion, which is why Stress is high while Tail is not. Two unpriced stacks sit between this assessment and the reopen. The first is the Gulf: an Iranian commercial vessel was struck near Qeshm Island in the Strait of Hormuz late Saturday, killing one and wounding four, and Iran and GCC foreign ministers are due to meet in Salalah on Monday on a joint Oman-Iran shipping route through the strait, with Bahrain having said it will not attend. That meeting is genuinely two-sided: an arrangement would ease the crude premium, a breakdown would tighten it. The second is Nasdaq-specific, after Anthropic and OpenAI leadership called for pacing the rate of AI capability advancement; reporting since frames the likely effect as short-term pressure on chip stocks rather than a broken AI trade, which limits the one-way potential. Cross-asset context from the latest completed session shows aligned positive breadth, seven of eight megacaps higher and a firm semiconductor complex, but that is delayed latest-session context, not live structure, and it is not treated as evidence of a current one-way path. With no observable price path, Tail is held at the low end and the conditional risk is expressed as a narrow flagged window around the reopen rather than as a broad shutdown.

lookbackSummary: All 24 preceding published hours were available and uniformly green with the mapped state EA_ON. Tail held flat at 6 from late Saturday through the overnight hours, then drifted up from 05:00 UTC to 17 by 15:00 UTC as the weekend ran toward the futures reopen, easing to 16 and then stepping to 17 and 18 across the final three hours. Stress rose steadily from 53 to 75 as the pre-FOMC rates and energy backdrop accumulated, the dominant mode stayed normal throughout, and Confidence held near 86 before stepping down to the low 70s from 16:00 UTC as the weekend evidence gap widened.
outlookSummary: The window splits into three phases. Until 22:00 UTC the CME equity complex is closed and no price path can form, so Tail holds in the low band and rises only as a forward allowance into the reopen. The 21:00-02:00 UTC stretch spanning the Globex reopen is the concentrated conditional risk point, where two unpriced stacks - the Gulf shipping escalation and the AI-pacing debate - can reprice into the thinnest liquidity of the week; Tail enters the watch band there as a gap allowance, not as an observed move, and the specific invalidation to watch is repeated extension with shallow or failed pullbacks. From the Asian hours onward the base case is absorption of any gap and a return to two-way trade, with Tail decaying toward 16 through the European session and a second conditional uptick into the 13:30 UTC U.S. cash open, where any AI-sector repricing meets its deepest liquidity. Monday's U.S. calendar holds only routine bill auctions at 15:30 UTC, so residual risk is headline-driven, with crude the main transmission channel and the Salalah Iran-GCC meeting an unresolved two-sided checkpoint. Stress stays in the high band throughout because the underlying tension - a live hike debate, a 10-year near 5%, crude near $100 and two open headline stacks - does not resolve before Wednesday's FOMC.
